key_insight: The paper makes RUDE constitutive models more stable, thermodynamically admissible, and interpretable by using logarithmic input compression, split networks, and a differentiable Clausius–Duhem projection.
engineering_relevance: These improvements make data-driven rheology models more reliable for CFD and for predicting industrial polymer processing under unseen flow conditions.
method: Multi-mode RUDE backbone with frame-indifferent tensorial basis and neural-network corrections
Logarithmic compression of invariants plus split-network architecture to improve conditioning
Differentiable projection layer enforces the Clausius–Duhem inequality at each time step
evidence_signal: The models were trained on LAOS data and validated on unseen steady shear, transient stress growth, and extensional flows for both a synthetic multi-mode Giesekus model and an entangled silicone polymer melt.
watch_item: The added projection and multi-branch architecture may increase implementation complexity and require careful tuning for efficient deployment in large CFD workflows.
paper_title: Stable and Interpretable Multi-Mode Rheological Universal Differential Equations (mmRUDEs) for Data-Driven Constitutive Modeling
